body.intent: Builders and fixers reproduce flaky tests by generating CPU load on the shared host. On 2026-11-09 two nebari runs did it: 01M6Z1RG ran 8 'bash' busy loops, and 01M6Z5P4 (session 42a0d9da) ran 14 'sh -c while :; do :; done' loops. Each held the 4-core VM at load 16–22 for 15–30+ min and slowed every other live run; I stopped them by PID. Load-based repro also barely works: 45/45 passed under load, while a 500 ms injected delay on the suspected request reproduced 10/10 (nebari PR #90). The build/fix guidance (rhiza guide build, the rhiza-build and rhiza-review skills) should say: reproduce timing flakes by injecting a delay at the suspected race, never by busy loops or parallel stress on the host. Optionally the watchdog flags a run's descendant processes that sit at 100% CPU for minutes.
